header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Ava Martinez (CTO - AutomaHealth), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Jordan Lee (SRE), Meera Gupta (Product)
Recording: yes
Notes: Weekly PoC check-in focused on caching (prefix + KV cache), hit rates, prompt reuse strategy, and next steps for benchmarking and Dedicated sizing.
transcript:
00:00 Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll start in a minute. 00:10 Ava: yeah good morning, thanks Lena. 00:15 Marcus: Morning, Marcus here from Redwood, gonna run through the numbers we pulled from the staging cluster. 00:22 Samir: quick note, we had a spike in 8/16 where KVcache memory usage jumped, still investigating but wanted to flag. 00:30 Marcus: got it, we'll cover that. quick summary first - overall prefix hit rate improved from 12% to 28% after the initial prefix normalization you all pushed last week. however effective KV hit is still low at around 18% which explains the token cost being higher than expected. 00:50 Ava: ok 18% seems lower than we hoped, can you explain how that maps to end-user latency? 00:58 Marcus: yeah so the idea is when the prefix cache hits, we can reuse past kv state and skip earlier token generation - that drops p95 by about 150-300ms in our tests. with 18% KV hits you're only getting that benefit for a small fraction of requests. 01:15 Jordan: is that the same as prefix TTL? we set TTL to 30 minutes right now. 01:21 Marcus: correct TTL is 30m; short TTL means less chance to hit for users with sporadic sessions. also prefix normalization rules were conservative - we didn't combine some templated parts. 01:34 Meera: maybe i can give an example - our email subject templates include timestamps that vary every request which destroys prefix reuse. 01:42 Marcus: exactly, and we recommended last week a lightweight prompt rewrite: move volatile pieces into variables rather than inline text, e.g., replace timestamps with {{ts}} token. that bumped prefix reuse in sim. 01:56 Samir: about the KV memory spike - it looked like cache churn during a background sweep, possibly our pruning policy interacting with a big upload. 02:06 Marcus: could be. we saw a transient where dozens of new prefixes were added within 10 minutes which caused eviction thrash. 02:15 Ava: are you recommending larger cache sizes or different eviction policies? 02:20 Marcus: two levers: increase KV capacity for the Dedicated pilot so we can keep more prefixes in memory, and tune eviction to LRU with a small protection window for recently accessed prefixes. also increase prefix TTL from 30m to 2h for this workload to capture less-frequent revisit patterns. 02:38 Samir: if we increase TTL won't we grow memory usage significantly? 02:42 Marcus: yes, which is why we suggested profiling with the 10k sample prefixes first - that will give a projection. also the Dedicated pool can be configured with higher memory for the cache tier. 02:55 Jordan: do you have numbers for cost delta? like how much more memory vs token cost savings? 03:01 Marcus: approximate - if KV hits go from 18% to 45% we saw token cost drop ~22% in our sims because fewer tokens generated overall. the memory increase for KV was about 30% in that scenario; exacts will depend on average prefix size. 03:18 Ava: that's promising. what's the work to get us into Dedicated for the pilot? 03:22 Lena: we can spin a small Dedicated pool, Marcus will size it after we run the TTL=2h benchmark; pricing will be outlined in the PoC plan I'll send. 03:31 Meera: earlier you mentioned prefix normalization rules - can you share the rule set? 03:36 Marcus: yes, we'll share the rule doc; examples: strip iso timestamps, normalize user ids to tokens, collapse repeated list items into hashed signature. we've got a first pass in the shared drive. 03:49 Samir: another question - are tool calls and function-calling responses being cached? we have a dynamic call to an inventory service that changes per request. 03:58 Marcus: we only cache deterministic prefixes; for tool calls we mark those as non-cacheable unless the downstream response is stable or we provide a custom caching hook. right now inventory calls are non-cacheable so they break reuse. 04:12 Ava: could we instead cache only the prompt up to tool call and then resume? 04:17 Marcus: yes, that's the recommended pattern: cache the prefix up to the tool invocation, then rehydrate after the tool result; that preserves KV usefulness for earlier tokens. 04:28 Jordan: regarding the KV spike on 8/16 - i can share metrics from our side, were there any backend restarts? 04:34 Marcus: we had one rolling restart during deployment window 8/16 at 03:00 UTC which may have forced keys to be ejected then reloaded; that could correlate. 04:42 Samir: ok we'll correlate logs. 04:45 Lena: quick pivot to prompts - we noticed several prompt templates embed whole JSON blobs which changes every run, low reuse. any guidance? 04:53 Marcus: yes flattening is key; pass JSON as a variable blob instead of inline, or hash stable keys only. also consider summarizing repeated context into a short-vector cached doc - Redwood supports embedding-based cache too but for this PoC we're focusing on prefix/KV. 05:08 Meera: you said embedding-cache integration exists? what's the difference in hit behavior? 05:13 Marcus: embedding cache is similarity-based; it's great for semantic reuse but not for exact prefix reuse. hit rates will look different; prefix hits are binary matches, embed hits require threshold tuning. 05:25 Ava: do you have recommended thresholds? 05:27 Marcus: start at cosine 0.85 for this domain, but we'll validate. 05:33 Samir: any concern about stale data with longer TTLs? our use case shows content updates hourly and some prefixes tie to up-to-date inventory. 05:42 Marcus: that's why an hybrid approach - shorter TTL for inventory-related prefixes and longer TTL for static templates. you can tag prefixes as volatile. we can expose prefix tagging in the config. 05:55 Meera: good. what's the next test you want us to run? 05:59 Marcus: run the benchmark with: TTL 2h for templated prefixes, TTL 15min for volatile ones, 200k synthetic requests reflecting your session distribution (we'll supply generator), and collect p50/p95, token cost, KV hit rate and memory usage. 06:15 Samir: timeline ok. i'll upload sample prefixes and run staging tests. 06:19 Jordan: ops will monitor memory. 06:22 Lena: next steps recap - Marcus shares config + dashboard, Samir uploads prefixes, Redwood runs benchmark and Lena sends pricing. any other blockers? 06:33 Ava: none from engineering side. 06:35 Marcus: ok i'll also add a note about fallback policy - if KV not available we can route to lower-cost model variant with graceful degradation. 06:44 Meera: that sounds helpful for production. 06:47 Lena: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invite for next review and post the PoC plan. 06:53 Ava: thanks everyone. 06:55 Meeting ends.

Summary:
- Prefix hit rate improved to ~28% after normalization but KV hit rate remains ~18%.
- Recommendations: increase prefix TTL to 2h for templates, tune eviction to LRU with recent-protection, tag volatile prefixes, and hybrid TTLs.
- Actions: share dashboard, run TTL=2h benchmark with 200k requests, upload 10k sample prefixes, and prepare Dedicated sizing/pricing.

References/links mentioned:

- Dashboard export: will be attached to the CRM
